item.title: US struck Isfahan ammo depot with bunker busters
item.description:
The United States struck a large ammunition depot in the Iranian city of Isfahan with a high volume of 2,000-pound penetrator munitions, according to a U.S. official cited by The Wall Street Journal. The strike triggered a chain of secondary explosions that lit up the night sky, with footage of towering fireballs circulating widely after President Trump shared an uncaptioned video of the attack on his Truth Social platform on Sunday evening. The Wall Street Journal confirmed the footage depicted the Isfahan operation.

The strike is the latest in more than a month of sustained U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran, launched on February 28 under what the Israel Defense Forces have termed "Operation Roaring Lion". Since then, more than 15,000 Iranian targets have been hit, according to the IDF, with the daily strike tempo declining from roughly 1,000 targets in the opening days to fewer than 100.

item.title: Trump willing to end Iran war without reopening Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
President Donald Trump has told aides he is willing to conclude the U.S. military campaign against Iran even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed to commercial shipping, The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, a move that could leave Tehran with lasting leverage over one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints.

The shift signals a recalibration of American war aims as the conflict, dubbed Operation Epic Fury, enters its fifth week. In recent discussions, Trump and his advisers concluded that attempting to force the strait open would extend the fighting beyond his preferred four-to-six-week timeline, according to administration officials cited by the Journal. Instead, Washington plans to focus on its stated objectives — degrading Iran's naval and missile capabilities — while pursuing diplomatic channels to persuade Tehran to restore maritime traffic.

item.title: Asian nations rush to buy Russian crude as Iran war chokes oil supply
item.description:
A growing number of Asian countries are turning to Russia for crude oil as the U.S.-Israeli military conflict with Iran continues to choke off energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, triggering what the International Energy Agency has called the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market."

The Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, and Sri Lanka have all signaled interest in purchasing Russian crude in recent weeks, joining established buyers China and India in a regional competition for barrels that analysts warn may soon outstrip what Moscow can deliver.

item.title: Data centers warm nearby land by up to 16°F, Cambridge study finds
item.description: The sprawling data centers powering artificial intelligence are creating localized "heat islands" that raise surface temperatures by an average of 3.6 degrees Fahrenheit — and up to 16.4 degrees in extreme cases — affecting an estimated 340 million people worldwide, according to new research from the University of Cambridge.

item.title: Gold climbs on report Trump may end Iran war
item.description: Gold prices climbed on Monday after a Wall Street Journal report that President Donald Trump told aides he is willing to end the U.S. military campaign against Iran, even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed. The gains extended into early Asian trading on Tuesday, with the metal also buoyed by Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's comments at Harvard University that eased fears of an imminent interest rate hike.

item.title: Australia, Indonesia probe tech giants over under-16 bans
item.description: Australia and Indonesia are both cracking down on major technology companies this week for failing to enforce new laws banning children under 16 from social media, in a coordinated global push to hold platforms accountable for youth safety online.

item.title: Global banks turn to Chinese stocks as Iran war roils markets
item.description: As the month-long U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran roils global markets and sends oil prices soaring, Chinese equities — and the country's dominant renewable energy sector in particular — have emerged as a rare bright spot for investors seeking refuge from the turmoil.

item.title: Hegseth calls upcoming days 'decisive' in Iran war
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday described the "upcoming days" as decisive in the month-long U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, pointing to widespread desertions within Tehran's armed forces and the degradation of its military capabilities as signs that the conflict is approaching a turning point.

item.title: Trump tells allies to 'take' Strait of Hormuz themselves
item.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his pressure on reluctant allies on Tuesday, posting on Truth Social that countries struggling with jet fuel shortages caused by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz should either purchase American oil or seize control of the waterway themselves.

"All of those countries that can't get jet fuel because of the Strait of Hormuz, like the United Kingdom, which refused to get involved in the decapitation of Iran, I have a suggestion for you: Number 1, buy from the US, we have plenty, and Number 2, build up some delayed courage, go to the Strait, and just TAKE IT," Trump wrote, singling out nations that declined to join U.S. strikes against Iran. He added that the United States "won't be there to help you anymore" and that allies would need to learn "how to fight for yourself".

item.title: U.S., Israel strike Isfahan and Tehran on Day 32 of Iran war
item.description: As the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran entered its 32nd day on Tuesday, powerful explosions rocked both Tehran and the central city of Isfahan in what appeared to be some of the most intense aerial bombardments since hostilities began on February 28. The escalation came alongside fresh Iranian retaliatory strikes across the region and a parallel diplomatic push led by Pakistan to bring Washington and Tehran to the negotiating table.

item.title: King Charles confirms first US state visit as monarch
item.description:
Buckingham Palace announced on Tuesday that King Charles III and Queen Camilla will undertake a state visit to the United States in late April, marking the first trip to America by a British monarch since Queen Elizabeth II's visit in 2007.

The visit, made at the invitation of President Donald Trump and on the advice of the British government, will celebrate the 250th anniversary of American independence — a milestone with particular resonance given that the U.S. declared independence during the reign of Charles's ancestor King George III.

item.title: Fourth Greek tanker crosses Hormuz despite Iran blockade
item.description:
The Greek-controlled Suezmax tanker Pola has successfully crossed the Strait of Hormuz, becoming the fourth vessel managed by Athens-based Dynacom Tankers Management Ltd. to navigate the chokepoint since the US and Israel launched military strikes against Iran on February 28, according to Bloomberg.

The Pola switched off its Automatic Identification System in the Persian Gulf on March 10 and reappeared on Monday in the eastern Indian Ocean near Indonesia's Sumatra island, vessel tracking data compiled by Bloomberg showed. The tanker, laden with roughly 1 million barrels of crude, is en route to Thailand, according to intelligence firm Kpler.

item.title: China verifies Mach 6 engine prototype after 30 years
item.description: Chinese researchers have completed and experimentally verified a prototype of a novel air-breathing propulsion system that can accelerate from a dead stop to more than six times the speed of sound, according to a report by the South China Morning Post on Sunday. The engine, called the "contra-rotary ramjet," represents over three decades of development and could reshape the design of future fighter jets and hypersonic missiles.

item.title: France denies blocking US military overflights after Trump threatens 'USA will remember'
item.description: French officials on Tuesday rejected President Donald Trump's assertion that Paris had blocked American military planes from crossing its airspace, clarifying that its overflight policy for U.S. aircraft remains unchanged even as it acknowledged refusing a specific weekend request to transport weapons to Israel.

item.title: Trump warns European allies after Italy, France block US military access
item.description: A widening rift between the United States and its European allies deepened on Tuesday as Italy and France took steps to block American military operations from their territory, prompting President Donald Trump to warn that "the USA won't be there to help you anymore." The escalating dispute over European involvement in the month-old US-Israeli military campaign against Iran is straining the NATO alliance while a parallel energy crisis rattles the continent's economy.

item.title: Indonesia rations fuel as Iran war drives oil prices higher
item.description: Indonesia announced fuel rationing on Tuesday as the month-old US-Israel military campaign against Iran continues to choke global energy supplies, with Brent crude trading above $100 a barrel and no diplomatic resolution in sight.

item.title: NASA's Artemis II moon mission set to launch Wednesday
item.description: NASA is hours away from launching the first crewed mission to the moon in more than half a century, with Navy Captain Victor Glover at the controls. The Artemis II mission is scheduled to lift off on Wednesday, April 1, at 6:24 p.m. EDT from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, sending four astronauts on an approximately 10-day journey around the moon and back.

item.title: Trump says US will finish Iran war in 'two to three weeks'
item.description:
President Donald Trump estimated on Tuesday that the United States would be finished with its military campaign against Iran in "two to three weeks," the latest in a series of shifting timelines as the conflict enters its second month with no clear exit strategy in sight.

The remarks came as the Pentagon deployed B-52 bombers over Iranian airspace for the first time since Operation Epic Fury began on February 28, a move Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine said was possible because U.S. and Israeli forces had dismantled Iran's air defense capabilities to such an extent that the slower aircraft could now operate safely. Trump also signaled a retreat from one of his stated objectives, telling aides he is willing to end the war even if the Strait of Hormuz — a chokepoint for roughly 20 percent of the world's oil supply — remains largely closed, according to The Wall Street Journal.

item.title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz will 'automatically' reopen when US exits Iran war
item.description:
President Trump declared Tuesday that the month-long U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran "won't last much longer" and that the Strait of Hormuz will reopen on its own once American forces withdraw, even as Iran's government flatly denied any negotiations are underway to end the conflict.

In a phone interview with the New York Post published on March 31, Trump framed the U.S. mission narrowly. "My primary responsibility was to ensure they don't possess a nuclear weapon. They will not acquire a nuclear weapon. Once we depart, the strait will automatically open," he said. He added that Iran "has no power remaining" and suggested that countries reliant on the waterway should "take the initiative to open it" themselves.

item.title: UK, Syria pledge to work with allies to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: As the war between the United States and Israel on one side and Iran on the other enters its fifth week, UN Secretary-General António Guterres has intensified his calls for all parties to pull back from the brink, warning that the conflict has spiraled "out of control" and risks devastating consequences for civilians and the global economy alike. His appeals come as diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — closed by Iran since early March — gain new urgency, with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa pledging on Tuesday to "work with others to restore freedom of navigation" through the critical waterway.
